lesson.titleZh: 向某人請教／請教某人的意見

examples.en: I often pick my brother’s brains.
examples.zh: 我經常向哥哥請教。

examples.en: The students picked their teacher’s brains.
examples.zh: 學生向老師請教。

meaning.en: To ask somebody who knows a great deal about a subject for information, advice, ideas or an opinion.
meaning.zh: 向對某個範疇有豐富知識或經驗的人請教，以取得有用的資料、意見、建議或想法。
naturalZh: 請某人分享經驗或想法

register.summaryEn: conversations between friends or colleagues; workplace discussions; messages and informal emails; meetings and workshops; conversations with teachers, advisers or experienced relatives.
register.summaryZh: 這個表達屬於非正式語域，特別適合朋友、同事、老師、顧問或家人之間的對話。
contextsEn: conversations with teachers, advisers or experienced relatives
register.formalEn: In formal correspondence, expressions such as seek your advice, consult you or ask for your professional opinion may be more suitable.
register.formalZh: 在正式信件中，seek your advice、consult you 或 ask for your professional opinion 通常較為合適。

fixedVariable.fixedEn: Keep the fixed words and word order shown in the source expression.
fixedVariable.fixedZh: 保留原檔目標表達中的固定字詞及字序。
fixedVariable.variableEn: Change only the verb form, possessive, tense or surrounding grammar permitted by the source patterns.
fixedVariable.variableZh: 只按照原檔句式改變動詞形式、所有格、時態或前後文法。

forms.example: I often pick my brother’s brains.

forms.form: Subject + can / could / should / may / will + pick + possessive + brains.
Subject + want / need / plan / hope + to pick + possessive + brains.
forms.example: I want to pick your brains about something.

forms.form: Can / Could / May I + pick + your brains...?
forms.example: Can I pick your brains about choosing a laptop?
The students are picking the guest speaker’s brains.

forms.form: Subject + have / has / had + picked + possessive + brains.
forms.example: I have already picked my mentor’s brains.
Picking my cousin’s brains helped me plan the trip.

forms.form: To pick + possessive + brains, + subject + verb...
forms.example: To pick the chef’s brains, we invited her to lunch.

forms.form: have a chance / opportunity / time + to pick + possessive + brains
forms.example: The workshop gave us a chance to pick the expert’s brains.

specificForms.titleZh: 句式一：一般限定動詞片語
specificForms.descriptionEn: This is the simplest complete structure.
specificForms.descriptionZh: 這是最基本的完整句式。

examples.en: I often pick my brother’s brains.
examples.zh: 我經常向哥哥請教。

examples.en: The students picked their teacher’s brains.
examples.zh: 學生向老師請教。

examples.en: Rachel picks her colleague’s brains whenever she needs a fresh idea.
examples.zh: 每當麗素需要新想法時，她都會向同事請教。

specificForms.formula: Subject + can / could / should / may / will + pick + possessive + brains.
specificForms.descriptionEn: After a modal verb, use the base form pick.
specificForms.descriptionZh: 情態動詞後必須使用原形 pick。

examples.en: We could pick Daniel’s brains.
examples.zh: 我們可以向丹尼爾請教。

examples.en: You should pick your coach’s brains before the competition.
examples.zh: 你應該在比賽前向教練請教。

examples.en: I may pick her brains tomorrow.
examples.zh: 我明天可能會向她請教。

specificForms.formula: Subject + want / need / plan / hope + to pick + possessive + brains.
specificForms.descriptionEn: The infinitive marker to belongs to the surrounding grammar. It is not part of the idiom.
specificForms.descriptionZh: 接在 Want、Need、Plan 或 Hope 之後不定詞標記 to 屬於外圍句法，並不是慣用語的固定部分。

examples.en: I want to pick your brains about something.
examples.zh: 我想就一件事向你請教。

examples.en: We need to pick the manager’s brains before deciding.
examples.zh: 我們作出決定前需要向經理請教。

examples.en: They plan to pick the designer’s brains tomorrow.
examples.zh: 他們計劃明天向設計師請教。

specificForms.titleZh: 句式四：禮貌問題及請求
specificForms.formula: Can / Could / May I + pick + your brains...?
specificForms.descriptionEn: The past form picked after would it be all right if does not necessarily refer to past time. It helps make the request less direct.
specificForms.descriptionZh: 在 would it be all right if 後使用 picked，並不一定表示過去時間，而是令請求較為委婉。

examples.en: Can I pick your brains about choosing a laptop?
examples.zh: 我可以就選擇手提電腦向你請教嗎？

examples.en: Could I pick your brains for a few minutes?
examples.zh: 我可以用幾分鐘向你請教一下嗎？

examples.en: Would it be all right if I picked your brains?
examples.zh: 我向你請教一下，可以嗎？

specificForms.descriptionEn: Use this form when the discussion is happening or was happening around a particular time.
specificForms.descriptionZh: 當請教過程正在某個時間進行時，可以使用這個句式。

examples.en: The students are picking the guest speaker’s brains.
examples.zh: 學生正在向嘉賓講者請教。

examples.en: I was picking my cousin’s brains about travelling alone.
examples.zh: 我當時正在向表哥請教獨自旅行的事情。

specificForms.formula: Subject + have / has / had + picked + possessive + brains.
specificForms.descriptionEn: Source grammar frame: Subject + have / has / had + picked + possessive + brains.
specificForms.descriptionZh: 原檔列出的句法框架：Subject + have / has / had + picked + possessive + brains。

examples.en: I have already picked my mentor’s brains.
examples.zh: 我已經向導師請教過。

examples.en: She had picked the engineer’s brains before the meeting.
examples.zh: 她在會議前已向工程師請教過。

examples.en: By Friday, we hope to have picked the coach’s brains.
examples.zh: 我們希望星期五前已向教練請教。

specificForms.titleZh: 句式七：以 Picking 開始的動名詞結構
specificForms.descriptionEn: The act of asking for knowledge or advice becomes the subject or complement of the sentence.
specificForms.descriptionZh: 整個請教行為可以成為句子的主語或補語。

examples.en: Picking my cousin’s brains helped me plan the trip.
examples.zh: 向表哥請教有助我規劃旅程。

examples.en: She spent an hour picking the engineer’s brains.
examples.zh: 她花了一小時向工程師請教。

specificForms.titleZh: 句式八：表示目的的不定詞
specificForms.formula: To pick + possessive + brains, + subject + verb...
specificForms.descriptionEn: The purpose clause is optional surrounding information. The core expression remains pick his brains.
specificForms.descriptionZh: 目的片語屬於可選的外圍資料。 核心表達仍然只是 pick his brains。

examples.en: To pick the chef’s brains, we invited her to lunch.
examples.zh: 為了向廚師請教，我們邀請她共進午餐。

examples.en: I called Daniel to pick his brains.
examples.zh: 我致電丹尼爾向他請教。

specificForms.titleZh: 句式九：機會或准許結構
specificForms.formula: have a chance / opportunity / time + to pick + possessive + brains
specificForms.descriptionEn: These nouns and verbs create the surrounding grammar. They are not fixed parts of the idiom.
specificForms.descriptionZh: 這些名詞及動詞只是建立外圍句法，並非慣用語的固定部分。

examples.en: The workshop gave us a chance to pick the expert’s brains.
examples.zh: 工作坊讓我們有機會向專家請教。

examples.en: The architect let us pick her brains.
examples.zh: 建築師讓我們向她請教。

examples.en: I picked her brains about the interview.
examples.zh: 我就面試的事情向她請教。

benefits.en: The idiomatic version makes it clearer that Daniel has useful knowledge or experience.
benefits.zh: 慣用語版本更清楚地表示丹尼爾擁有有用的知識或經驗。

benefits.titleZh: 比 Ask 表達更多意思
benefits.en: the speaker needs information or advice; the other person knows more about the subject; the speaker asks questions to learn from that person.
benefits.zh: 這個慣用語同時表達說話者需要資料或意見、對方較熟悉該主題，以及說話者透過提問向對方學習。

benefits.titleEn: It Is Useful for Friendly Professional Conversations
benefits.en: It sounds cooperative without being extremely formal.
benefits.zh: 我可以就這個顧客問題向你請教嗎？ 更改網站前，我們應該向設計師請教。 這個表達帶有合作語氣，同時不會過於正式。

examples.en: Could I pick your brains about this customer problem?
examples.zh: 我可以就這個顧客問題向你請教嗎？

examples.en: We should pick the designer’s brains before changing the website.
examples.zh: 更改網站前，我們應該向設計師請教。

benefits.titleEn: It Helps Make Requests Sound Conversational
benefits.en: The second version is shorter and more natural among colleagues or people who already know one another.
benefits.zh: 在同事或彼此認識的人之間，第二個版本較簡短自然。

benefits.titleEn: It Works in Several Grammar Patterns
benefits.en: a subject; a modal verb; an infinitive; a request structure; a time clause; an opportunity phrase; a gerund construction.
benefits.zh: 這個慣用語可以放在主語後、情態動詞後、不定詞結構中、請求句中、時間分句中、機會結構中或動名詞結構中。

benefits.en: Giving a topic and a reasonable time frame helps the listener understand what assistance is being requested.
benefits.zh: 我可以用五分鐘，就面試的事情向你請教嗎？ 提供主題和合理的時間範圍，可以讓對方清楚知道你需要甚麼協助。

examples.en: Could I pick your brains for five minutes about the interview?
examples.zh: 我可以用五分鐘，就面試的事情向你請教嗎？

origin.statusEn: Exact Origin Unknown; Likely Gradual Metaphorical Development
origin.statusZh: 確切來源不明；很可能是逐漸形成的比喻用法

history.en: Today, the British expression pick someone’s brains means asking a knowledgeable person for information, advice, ideas or an opinion. It is informal and commonly used in conversation.
history.zh: 今天，英式表達 pick someone’s brains 表示向熟悉某個範疇的人請教，以取得資料、意見、建議或想法。 它屬於非正式表達，常見於日常對話。

origin.memoryEn: Imagine selecting useful ideas from a person’s store of knowledge—not touching a real brain.
origin.memoryZh: 想像你正在從一個人的知識庫中挑選有用想法，而不是真正接觸大腦。

rules.titleZh: 規則一：使用英式複數形式 Brains
rules.zh: 使用英式複數形式 Brains

rules.en: Unless the person is genuinely unknown, someone’s should be replaced with the correct possessor.
rules.zh: 除非被請教者的身分確實不明，否則必須把 someone’s 改成正確的所有格。

rules.titleEn: Use a Possessive, Not an Object Pronoun
rules.titleZh: 規則三：使用所有格，不使用受詞代名詞
rules.en: Use a Possessive, Not an Object Pronoun
rules.zh: 使用所有格，不使用受詞代名詞

rules.titleEn: The Other Person Should Have Useful Knowledge
rules.titleZh: 規則四：對方應具備有用的知識或經驗
rules.en: If Daniel has no relevant knowledge, the situation does not naturally license the idiom.
rules.zh: 丹尼爾有多年維修單車的經驗，所以我向他請教煞車問題。 如果丹尼爾沒有相關知識，這個情境便不適合使用該慣用語。

examples.en: Daniel has repaired bicycles for years, so I picked his brains about my brakes.
examples.zh: 丹尼爾有多年維修單車的經驗，所以我向他請教煞車問題。

rules.titleEn: It Means Asking for Knowledge, Not Copying
rules.titleZh: 規則五：意思是請教，不是抄襲
rules.en: Work; secretly copying somebody’s homework; stealing a completed report; taking somebody’s private files; forcing somebody to reveal confidential information.
rules.zh: 它通常不表示偷偷抄功課、偷取報告、拿走私人檔案或強迫別人洩露機密。

rules.titleEn: Preserve the Topic When It Matters
rules.titleZh: 規則六：必要時保留請教主題
rules.en: The shorter sentence can be natural in an established conversation, but the answer key should normally preserve the important topic.
rules.zh: 較短的句子在已有清楚語境的對話中可以成立，但獨立答案通常應保留重要主題。

rules.titleZh: 規則七：保留時態及情態
rules.en: The incorrect answer changes a possibility into a completed action.
rules.zh: 錯誤答案把可能採取的行動改成已完成的事實。

rules.titleZh: 規則八：適當時使用禮貌句式
rules.en: When speaking to a teacher, expert, senior colleague or somebody giving their time freely, a request form is often more considerate.
rules.zh: 當對方是老師、專家、資深同事或正在抽空幫忙的人，使用請求句通常更有禮貌。

rules.titleEn: Do Not Interpret the Expression Literally
rules.titleZh: 規則九：不要按字面理解
rules.en: The idiom does not describe physically touching, opening or removing a brain. It refers figuratively to obtaining useful knowledge through conversation.
rules.zh: 這個慣用語不是指真正接觸、打開或取出人的大腦。 它以比喻方式表示透過交談取得有用知識。

rules.titleZh: 規則十：不要加入不必要的意思重複
rules.en: The second clause repeats the meaning already expressed by the idiom.
rules.zh: 第二個分句重複了慣用語已經表達的意思。

rules.titleZh: 規則十一：About 片語並非必須
rules.en: The second sentence simply supplies the topic. Do not teach pick someone’s brains about as though every answer must contain about.
rules.zh: 第二句只是補充請教的主題。 不要把 pick someone’s brains about 當成每個答案都必須使用的完整固定形式。

rules.titleEn: Do Not Confuse It with Other “Brain”
rules.titleZh: 規則十二：不要與其他包含 Brain 的表達混淆
rules.en: Expressions rack one’s brains be the brains behind something These expressions have different meanings and grammar.
rules.zh: 不要與其他包含 Brain 的表達混淆 pick someone’s brains 向某人請教努力思考或回想 be the brains behind something 是某項計劃背後的主要策劃者這些表達的意思及句法均不相同。

instructions.en: Rewrite or respond to each item using pick someone’s brains.
instructions.zh: 使用 pick someone’s brains 改寫句子或完成回應。

questions.prompt: Olivia knows a great deal about indoor plants. I asked her why mine were dying.
questions.promptZh: 奧莉花對室內植物十分熟悉。我向她請教自己的植物為甚麼正在枯萎。
questions.answer: I picked Olivia’s brains about why my plants were dying.
questions.answerZh: 我向奧莉花請教自己的植物為甚麼正在枯萎。
questions.targetMeaning: To ask somebody who knows a great deal about a subject for information, advice, ideas or an opinion.

questions.prompt: Daniel knows a great deal about computers. We asked him which laptop would suit us.
questions.promptZh: 丹尼爾對電腦十分熟悉。我們向他請教哪一部手提電腦適合我們。
questions.answer: We picked Daniel’s brains about which laptop would suit us.
questions.answerZh: 我們向丹尼爾請教哪一部手提電腦適合我們。
questions.targetMeaning: To ask somebody who knows a great deal about a subject for information, advice, ideas or an opinion.

questions.prompt: My aunt has run a café for many years. I asked her for advice before opening mine.
questions.promptZh: 我的姨母經營咖啡店多年。我在開店前向她請教。
questions.answer: Before opening my café, I picked my aunt’s brains about running one.
questions.answerZh: 開設咖啡店前，我向姨母請教經營方法。
questions.targetMeaning: To ask somebody who knows a great deal about a subject for information, advice, ideas or an opinion.

questions.prompt: The teacher knew exactly what the examination required. The students asked her for advice.
questions.promptZh: 老師非常了解考試要求。學生向她請教。
questions.answer: The students picked their teacher’s brains about the examination.
questions.answerZh: 學生向老師請教考試的事情。
questions.targetMeaning: To ask somebody who knows a great deal about a subject for information, advice, ideas or an opinion.

questions.prompt: Ava has visited Osaka several times. I asked her where I should stay.
questions.promptZh: 艾娃到訪大阪多次。我向她請教應該住在哪裏。

questions.answerZh: 為了在大阪找到合適的住宿地點，我向艾娃請教。
questions.targetMeaning: To ask somebody who knows a great deal about a subject for information, advice, ideas or an opinion.

questions.prompt: Ben has repaired bicycles for years. Leo asked him how to fix the brakes.
questions.promptZh: 本有多年維修單車的經驗。里奧向他請教如何修理煞車。
questions.answer: Leo picked Ben’s brains about repairing the bicycle brakes.
questions.answerZh: 里奧向本請教如何修理單車煞車。
questions.targetMeaning: To ask somebody who knows a great deal about a subject for information, advice, ideas or an opinion.

questions.prompt: My neighbour grows excellent vegetables. I want to ask her how she does it.
questions.promptZh: 我的鄰居種植的蔬菜非常好。我想向她請教種植方法。
questions.answer: I want to pick my neighbour’s brains about growing vegetables.
questions.answerZh: 我想向鄰居請教種植蔬菜的方法。
questions.targetMeaning: To ask somebody who knows a great deal about a subject for information, advice, ideas or an opinion.

questions.prompt: Our manager understands our customers very well. We need her advice about what they want.
questions.promptZh: 我們的經理十分了解顧客。我們需要請教她顧客想要甚麼。
questions.answer: We need to pick our manager’s brains about what customers want.
questions.answerZh: 我們需要向經理請教顧客想要甚麼。
questions.targetMeaning: To ask somebody who knows a great deal about a subject for information, advice, ideas or an opinion.

questions.prompt: My sister works at a hotel. I will ask her for advice about my hotel interview next week.
questions.promptZh: 我的姐姐在酒店工作。我下星期會向她請教酒店面試的事情。
questions.answer: Next week, I will pick my sister’s brains about the hotel interview.
questions.answerZh: 下星期，我會向姐姐請教酒店面試的事情。
questions.targetMeaning: To ask somebody who knows a great deal about a subject for information, advice, ideas or an opinion.

questions.prompt: Our grandfather knows a great deal about our family’s history. We spent lunchtime asking him questions.
questions.promptZh: 祖父十分了解家族歷史。我們在午膳期間向他提出了很多問題。
questions.answer: During lunch, we picked our grandfather’s brains about our family history.
questions.answerZh: 午膳期間，我們向祖父請教家族歷史。
questions.targetMeaning: To ask somebody who knows a great deal about a subject for information, advice, ideas or an opinion.

questions.prompt: You know a great deal about cameras. May I ask you for advice about choosing one?
questions.promptZh: 你對相機十分熟悉。我可以向你請教如何選擇相機嗎？
questions.answer: Can I pick your brains about choosing a camera?
questions.answerZh: 我可以就選擇相機向你請教嗎？
questions.targetMeaning: To ask somebody who knows a great deal about a subject for information, advice, ideas or an opinion.

questions.prompt: You have planned many holidays. May I ask for your opinion about this travel plan?
questions.promptZh: 你規劃過很多次旅行。我可以就這份旅遊計劃請教你的意見嗎？
questions.answer: Could I pick your brains about this travel plan?
questions.answerZh: 我可以就這份旅遊計劃請教你的意見嗎？
questions.targetMeaning: To ask somebody who knows a great deal about a subject for information, advice, ideas or an opinion.

questions.prompt: You have helped many people improve their CVs. Would it be acceptable for me to ask for your advice about mine?
questions.promptZh: 你曾協助很多人改善履歷。我向你請教自己的履歷，可以嗎？
questions.answer: Would it be all right if I picked your brains about my CV?
questions.answerZh: 我向你請教自己的履歷，可以嗎？
questions.targetMeaning: To ask somebody who knows a great deal about a subject for information, advice, ideas or an opinion.

questions.prompt: Rachel’s colleague always has useful teaching ideas. Rachel asks for those ideas whenever she plans a lesson.
questions.promptZh: 麗素的同事總有實用的教學想法。每當麗素規劃課堂時，她都會向同事請教。
questions.answer: Whenever she plans a lesson, Rachel picks her colleague’s brains for fresh ideas.
questions.answerZh: 每當麗素規劃課堂時，她都會向同事請教新想法。
questions.targetMeaning: To ask somebody who knows a great deal about a subject for information, advice, ideas or an opinion.

questions.prompt: The chef knows how to make the sauce properly. The trainees are asking him about it now.
questions.promptZh: 廚師知道如何正確製作醬汁。學員現在正在向他請教。
questions.answer: They are picking the chef’s brains about making the sauce.
questions.answerZh: 他們正在向廚師請教如何製作醬汁。
questions.targetMeaning: To ask somebody who knows a great deal about a subject for information, advice, ideas or an opinion.

questions.prompt: My mentor has helped many people change careers. I have asked her for advice several times.
questions.promptZh: 我的導師曾協助很多人轉行。我已經向她請教過幾次。
questions.answer: I have picked my mentor’s brains several times about changing careers.
questions.answerZh: 我已經數次向導師請教轉行的事情。
questions.targetMeaning: To ask somebody who knows a great deal about a subject for information, advice, ideas or an opinion.

questions.prompt: We are not certain which plan will work. We should ask a colleague who has done this before.
questions.promptZh: 我們不肯定哪個計劃可行。我們應該向曾處理過這種事情的同事請教。
questions.answer: Before deciding, we should pick an experienced colleague’s brains.
questions.answerZh: 作出決定前，我們應該向有經驗的同事請教。
questions.targetMeaning: To ask somebody who knows a great deal about a subject for information, advice, ideas or an opinion.

questions.prompt: Clara has completed the same application successfully. Ask her for advice if you are uncertain.
questions.promptZh: 嘉拉曾成功完成同一份申請。如果你不肯定，便向她請教。
questions.answer: If you are unsure about the application, pick Clara’s brains.
questions.answerZh: 如果你不肯定如何處理申請，便向嘉拉請教。
questions.targetMeaning: To ask somebody who knows a great deal about a subject for information, advice, ideas or an opinion.

questions.prompt: Priya organised last year’s school fair. Let us ask her for ideas about this year’s event.
questions.promptZh: 佩雅籌辦了去年的學校嘉年華。讓我們向她請教今年活動的想法。
